 JUDGMENT

The present case emanates from the first information statement of Sri.Srinivas S/o. Bhujangegowda on 5.06.2010 at 10.35 p.m., Basvanagudi Traffic Police Station registered in Crime No.204/2010 on receiving the documents in Crime No.68/ 2010.
2.

The informant claims to be residing in house No.#28, 3rd Main Road, 9th cross, Bapujinagar,
Mysuru Road, Bengaluru-26 and discharging duty as Police Constable with Badge No.P.C.7875 in Basavanagudi Police Station for about 1 year prior to the date of the incident.

On 2.06.2010, the informant along with PSI Sri.Nataraj.M, Sri.Sakarappa, PC 9802 and Sri.Gopalakrishna PC 6853 were deputed for tracking and taking action against the individuals driving in intoxicated condition.
The informant and other police officers were on duty from 10.00 pm on that day.
At about 10.45 p.m while on duty tracking such individuals had reached Diwan Madhavarao Road in front of Gunasheela Hospital and were discharging their duty.
At that time, a white car had come from Armugam Circle towards Diwan Madhavarao Road when the PSI had directed to stop the vehicle and to find out as to whether the driver was drunk or not.
The informant claims to have proceeded to use alcohometer on the driver and asked him to open the mouth.

The driver knowing that, the informant is a public servant, the informant in his uniform had pulled him by holding the uniform,
asked as to whether the informant was a doctor to examine him and threatened to show him as to what his power was.
The informant had then asked the driver to come before his superior officer.
The driver had then threatened the informant as to what he would do with him and on the seat had started the Car to run over him intentionally.
The informant claims to have attempted to save himself, but the driver was hell bent upon mowing the Car over him.

The informant somehow saving himself from being mowed over had fallen on the bonnet of the Car colliding his head to the windshield causing blood stained injury and had also sustained injury on his legs and hands.
The registration number of that Car was KA.05-MF.8444.
the driver had then drove the car from the place.
The other officials had helped the informant to be shifted to the hospital.
3. The learned II ACMM, Bengaluru City, on receipt of the final report from the Police, took cognizance of the aforesaid offences against the accused and registered a case in C.C.No.16151/2011.

Complied with the requirements under Section 207 of Cr.P.C. and thereafter by an order dated 31.07.2015, committed the case to the Principal City Civil and Sessions Judge Court, Bengaluru,
under Section 209 of Cr.PC.
4.

After hearing both the sides, this Court has framed the charge against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 332, 353, 279, 333 of IPC and Contravention of Section 134 AB of the Motor Vehicles Act punishable under Section 187 of the Motor Vehicles Act, read over and explained the same in the language known to him and he pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
6.

In order to prove the case, the prosecution has got examined 10 witnesses as PW-1 to PW-10 and got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12 documents and got marked MOs.1 & 2.
7.
After closure of the prosecution evidence, the statement of the accused has been recorded under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
The accused has taken a plea of total denial and has not led any defence evidence.
8. Heard the arguments from the learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel appearing for the accused.
Perused the materials placed on record along with citations.

9. The learned counsel for the accused has relied upon the following rulings:
1. (1977) 2 SCC 124 in the case of Ram Das Vs State of Maharashtra.
2. (1977) 4 SCC 420 in the case of Bir Singh and others Vs State of Uttar Pradesh.
3. AIR 1980 SCC 1382 in the case of State (Delhi Administration) Vs V.C.Shukla and another.
4. 1971 SCC 436 in the case of Yudhishtir Vs The State of Madhya Pradesh.
5. 1979 Crl.L.J. 1332 in the case of Kanbi Purshottam Ladha Vs State of Gujarat.
I have gone through the above rulings.

10. The points that arise for my consideration are as follows:-
1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond a reasonable doubt that, the accused had driven the Hundai Verna Car bearing Reg.No.KA.05- MF.8444 on 2.06.2010 at 10.45 p.m on Diwan Madhdava Rao Road from Armugam Circle towards Diwan Madhavarao Road in front of Gunasheela Hospital in a manner so rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 279 of the Indian Penal Code ?

2. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond a reasonable doubt that, the accused on the above said date, time and place voluntarily caused hurt to CW.1 Sri.Srinivas PC-7875 being a public Basavanagudi P.S vs Vinith Kumar on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144474622/
3 servant in the discharge of his duty as such public servant, with intent to prevent or deter that person from discharging his duty as such public servant on that day at that time and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 332 of the Indian Penal Code?
3. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond a reasonable doubt that, the accused on the above said date, time, caused hurt to CW.1 Sri.Srinivas PC-7875 so rash and negligent manner endangering his life and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec.337 of Indian Penal Code ?
4.

Whether the prosecution further proves beyond a reasonable doubt that, the accused on the above said date, time and place used criminal force by trying to mow the car over CW.1 Sri.Srinivas PC-7875 being a public servant in the execution and discharging his duty lawfully and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec.353 of Indian Penal Code ?

5. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond a reasonable doubt that, the accused on the above said date, time and place the accused had driven the Car bearing No.KA.05-MF.8444 voluntarily caused grievous hurt to CW.1 Sri.Srinivas, PC-7875 being a public servant in the discharge of his duty and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 333 of Indian Penal Code ?

6. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond a reasonable doubt that, the accused on the above said date, time and place, the accused had driven the Hundai Verna Car bearing Reg.No.KA.05-MF.8444 so rash and negligent manner endangering the life of CW.1 Sri.Srinivas,
PC-7875, Public Servant and failed to take all reasonable steps to secure medical attention to CW.1 by helping him to be taken to the nearest medical practitioner had contravened the Provision of Section 134 (a) of the Motor Vehicles Act and thereby committed offence punishable under Section 187 of the Motor Vehicles Act ?
7. What order ?

11. My findings on the above points are:-
Point Nos.1 to 4 & 6 : In the Affirmative.
Point No.5 : In the Negative,

Point No.7 : As per final order,

 REASONS 12.

Points Nos.1 to 6 : PW.1 Sri.Srinivas, ASI, KJ Police Station, victim and injured in this case had deposed on 29.10.2021 narrating the incident according to the recitals in the first information statement.
The witness recalls as to how he was treated by the accused while on duty, he was pulled by the uniform and then attempted to mow the car over the official.

The witness claims to have sustained injuries on the head, hands Basavanagudi P.S vs Vinith Kumar on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144474622/

The witness had stated that, he was treated as an inpatient for 3 days.
The witness claims to have lodged information with the police and had identified his signature on the first information statement.
Ex.P.1 is the first information statement and Ex.P.1(a) is the signature of the witness.
The witness is found to have stated that, he was first taken to the Bharathi Nursing Home and thereafter shifted to Sagar Hospital.
CWs.13 and 14 are said to have accompanied this witness to the hospital.
13. Ex.P.6 is the wound certificate issued by the Sagar Hospital that would reveal that, this witness was brought to the hospital by Sri.M.nataraj, P.S.I.
The witness claims that, he was out of conscious when he was taken to the hospital.
The witness had identified the car in the photographs at Ex.P.5.
The witness had identified the accused before the Court who had attempted to mow the car over him.
During the cross- examination of PW.1, an attempt was made to elicit to whether there were any documents to show that, he was on duty at the place on the date of incident.
There was barricades kept on the road.
The witness is found to have denied the suggestion that, it was dark and low visibility and that the witness had seen the accused for the first time before the Court.

Therefore,
it is clear that, the witness had seen the accused on that day and there was sufficient street light to identify the vehicle and the driver.
The witness was questioned about another person in the car.
This question would not be fatal to the prosecution as it is for the accused to disclose as to who else was there in the car.
When the informant had seen the accused and was capable of identifying, it is not a rule that, an identification parade is to be held.
It is not the defence that, the accused and this witness had known each other prior to the incident and this witness had malice intention against the accused.
While this witness was in the hospital, CW.2 had lodged information for the offence punishable under Sections 279, 337 of the Indian Penal Code.
PW.1 is found to have admitted the suggestion that, there was no animosity between this witness and the accused.
The credibility of the witness is not shaken after a thorough cross examination.
There is nothing to disbelieve the testimony of this witness.
It may be true that, a case was also registered earlier for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of the Indian Penal Code.
There is nothing that deters an Investigating Officer to investigate into all the offences that prima facie are made out from the facts in a particular case.

The witness was questioned about another person in the car.
This question would not be fatal to the prosecution as it is for the accused to disclose as to who else was there in the car.
When the informant had seen the accused and was capable of identifying, it is not a rule that, an identification parade is to be held.
It may be true that, a case was also registered earlier for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of the Indian Penal Code.
There is nothing that deters an Investigating Officer to investigate into all the offences that prima facie are made out from the facts in a particular case.

It is not the case of the accused that, there was any other accident involving this car, in which, there was damage to the car.
